endorsements.quote: The availability of AI-CDSS tools should not supersede the needs for patient–HCP interaction.

Understanding the principles and practice of AI-CDSS must be a core competency for medical school students and a focus for continuous professional development after qualification, with periodic recertification in this discipline.

unlisted_practices: Develop AI-CDSS with 'red flag' functionality that alerts users or HCPs to an urgent need for in-clinic review.
Include primary care physicians as key stakeholders in the development and implementation of AI-CDSS.
Make regulatory certification processes agile enough to evaluate AI systems that learn and change with each input or use.
Develop objective criteria to support risk categorisation of AI-CDSS under the EU AI Act.
Make the data underlying European market authorisation of AI-CDSS available for public scrutiny and representative of the diversity of the intended-use population.
Establish legal safeguards that protect the rights of people with diabetes, including data privacy and misuse, equally to those of commercial developers and healthcare stakeholders.
Adopt open data standards and standard APIs to enable interoperability between devices.
Design AI-CDSS to be adaptable across geographical regions and transparent to all relevant stakeholders.
Design RCT protocols to collect and report individualised treatment effects in addition to average treatment effects.
Train AI-CDSS on datasets that exclude bias by ethnicity, sex or socioeconomic status.
Give people with diabetes control over who receives their data and for what purpose, and stop blanket monetisation of patient data.

screen.reason: Delphi-based consensus statement and roadmap providing 14 recommendations for implementing AI-driven clinical decision support systems in diabetes care.
